Someone familiar with the subject should feel it intuitively, while others simply experience a masterful abstract composition. The design philosophy provides the aesthetic language. The deduced topic provides the soul - the quiet conceptual DNA woven invisibly into form, color, and composition.
    95	
    96	This is **VERY IMPORTANT**: The reference must be refined so it enhances the work's depth without announcing itself. Think like a jazz musician quoting another song - only those who know will catch it, but everyone appreciates the music.
    97

   100	## CANVAS CREATION
   101	
   102	With both the philosophy and the conceptual framework established, express it on a canvas. Take a moment to gather thoughts and clear the mind. Use the design philosophy created and the instructions below to craft a masterpiece, embodying all aspects of the philosophy with expert craftsmanship.
   103

   105	
   106	To create museum or magazine quality work, use the design philosophy as the foundation. Create one single page, highly visual, design-forward PDF or PNG output (unless asked for more pages). Generally use repeating patterns and perfect shapes. Treat the abstract philosophical design as if it were a scientific bible, borrowing the visual language of systematic observation—dense accumulation of marks, repeated elements, or layered patterns that build meaning through patient repetition and reward sustained viewing. Add sparse, clinical typography and systematic reference markers that suggest this could be a diagram from an imaginary discipline, treating the invisible subject with the same reverence typically reserved for documenting observable phenomena. Anchor the piece with simple phrase(s) or details positioned subtly, using a limited color palette that feels intentional and cohesive. Embrace the paradox of using analytical visual language to express ideas about human experience: the result should feel like an artifact that proves something ephemeral can be studied, mapped, and understood through careful attention. This is true art.

A punk venue poster might have larger, more aggressive type than a minimalist ceramics studio identity. Most of the time, font should be thin. All use of fonts must be design-forward and prioritize visual communication. Regardless of text scale, nothing falls off the page and nothing overlaps. Every element must be contained within the canvas boundaries with proper margins. Check carefully that all text, graphics, and visual elements have breathing room and clear separation. This is non-negotiable for professional execution. **IMPORTANT: Use different fonts if writing text. Search the `./canvas-fonts` directory. Regardless of approach, sophistication is non-negotiable.**

Make it appear as though someone at the absolute top of their field labored over every detail with painstaking care. Ensure the composition, spacing, color choices, typography - everything screams expert-level craftsmanship. Double-check that nothing overlaps, formatting is flawless, every detail perfect. 1	# JS Framework Benchmark: 5 Years of Browser Performance Testing
     2	
     3	## Overview
     4	
     5	The **JS Framework Benchmark** is the most widely referenced open-source benchmark for comparing JavaScript web frameworks on real-world DOM operations. Maintained by Stefan Krause and hosted on GitHub, it measures operations such as creating 1,000 rows, partial updates, row selection, swapping, removal, and startup time — all inside a real Chrome browser with controlled CPU throttling.
     6	
     7	Since its inception, the project has published **over 60 official result sets**, covering Chrome versions from **55 (circa 2017) all the way to 146 (mid-2026)**. Each result set captures dozens of frameworks — both keyed and non-keyed implementations — giving developers a consistent yardstick for performance.
     8	
     9	## Methodology Milestones
    10	
    11	The benchmark has undergone several important methodology changes that make **cross-version comparisons unreliable**:
    12	
    13	| Milestone | Chrome Version | Year | Description |
    14	|---|---|---|---|
    15	| Weighted Geometric Mean | 118 | 2023 | Overall score switched from arithmetic to weighted geometric mean |
    16	| CPU Throttling Adjustment | 118 | 2023 | Throttling factors recalibrated for more realistic load simulation |
    17	| Measurement Fine-Tuning | 118+ | 2023–present | Ongoing refinements to timing and driver instrumentation |
    18	| Keyed-Only Alternation | 139+ | 2025–2026 | Odd Chrome versions often benchmark keyed frameworks only |
    19	
    20	Because of these evolving parameters, the project explicitly warns: *"Comparisons across Chrome versions aren't always safe since the benchmark and its driver are constantly developing."*
    21	
    22	## Timeline of Official Runs
    23	
    24	The table below summarizes the distribution of official benchmark runs by year:
    25	
    26	| Year | Chrome Versions | Number of Runs | Notes |
    27	|---|---|---|---|
    28	| 2017–2019 | 55, 58, 62, 69 | 4 | Early era; hosted on stefankrause.net |
    29	| 2020 | 83 – 87 | 5 | Migrated to GitHub Pages |
    30	| 2021 | 88 – 96 | 9 | Steady monthly cadence established |
    31	| 2022 | 97 – 108 | 13 | Includes 2 Windows runs (Chrome 104) |
    32	| 2023 | 109 – 120 | 12 | Major methodology overhaul at Chrome 118 |
    33	| 2024 | 121 – 131 | 12 | Includes 1 Windows run (Chrome 121) |
    34	| 2025 | 132 – 143 | 12 | Most active year; alternating keyed-only runs |
    35	| 2026 | 144 – 146 | 3 (so far) | Latest: Chrome 146 on macOS |
    36	
    37	## Platform Coverage
    38	
    39	The vast majority of runs — **over 95%** — were executed on **macOS (OSX)**. Only two Windows-specific runs exist:
    40	
    41	- **Chrome 104 – Windows** (2022)
    42	- **Chrome 121 – Windows** (2024)
    43	
    44	This means the benchmark primarily reflects macOS + Chrome performance characteristics.
    45	
    46	## Key Takeaways for Developers
    47	
    48	1. **Compare within the same Chrome version.** Methodology and throttling differ across releases.
    49	2. **Consult the latest run** (currently Chrome 146) for the most up-to-date framework standings.
    50	3. **Understand keyed vs non-keyed modes.** Recent odd-numbered Chrome runs benchmark keyed frameworks only, while even-numbered runs include both.
    51	4. **60+ data points over 8 years** make this the longest-running, most comprehensive JS framework performance tracker available.
    52	5. **Weighted geometric mean** (since Chrome 118) gives a more balanced overall score than the previous arithmetic approach.

# Systemic Precision

## A Design Philosophy for the JS Framework Benchmark Poster

Space is organized like a control panel at midnight — every element serves a function, yet the whole breathes with deliberate rhythm. The dark canvas becomes the void of a terminal screen, where data glows with intention and every mark is a decision. This is not decoration applied to information; this is information made visible through the discipline of form.

Color is used surgically. Electric blues trace pathways of information across the composition, amber marks points of caution with the urgency of a warning light, and teal provides the cool authority of measured truth. The palette is restrained because restraint is the visual equivalent of accuracy — each hue earns its place through necessity, not whim. The interplay between these accents against the deep navy ground creates a luminosity that feels both technical and alive, as if the poster itself is powered.

Typography is treated as instrumentation. Monospaced glyphs carry the weight of raw data — numbers, versions, metrics — with the unimpeachable authority of source code. Clean sans-serifs provide structural hierarchy for headings and labels, their letterforms spaced with the exactitude of someone who understands that alignment is philosophy made visible. Text is sparse, never explanatory; it anchors what the visual architecture already communicates. Words appear as rare, powerful gestures integrated into the grid, never as paragraphs floating in space.

The timeline is the spine — a horizontal strip that anchors the entire composition, rendered with the density of a seismograph readout. Grid lines and dot patterns are not ornamental; they are the skeleton of understanding, revealing hidden order beneath years of complexity. Small marks accumulate into meaning through patient repetition, rewarding sustained viewing the way a masterfully engineered interface rewards a trained eye. Density reveals itself in layers.

Every proportion, every margin, every breath of negative space is the product of painstaking attention. The final work must appear as though it emerged from a laboratory where beauty and function are the same substance — meticulously crafted by someone at the absolute top of their field, labored over with the care of an instrument maker calibrating a precision tool. Nothing overlaps. Nothing is arbitrary. Everything is contained, measured, and true.

    return tuple(int(h[i:i+2], 16) for i in (1, 3, 5))

def rgb_to_hex(r, g, b):
    return f"#{r:02x}{g:02x}{b:02x}"

def blend_color(c1, c2, t):
    r1, g1, b1 = hex_to_rgb(c1)
    r2, g2, b2 = hex_to_rgb(c2)
    return rgb_to_hex(int(r1 + (r2-r1)*t), int(g1 + (g2-g1)*t), int(b1 + (b2-b1)*t))

    x, y = pos
    # Create glow layer
    glow = Image.new("RGBA", (W, H), (0, 0, 0, 0))
    gdraw = ImageDraw.Draw(glow)
    # Draw text multiple times with offset for glow
    for dx in range(-glow_radius, glow_radius+1, 2):

    glow = glow.filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(radius=6))
    img.paste(glow, (0, 0), glow)
    draw.text((x, y), text, font=font, fill=color)

# Timeline spine — thicker, more present

spine_left, spine_right = 160, W - 160
